'''Juan Bisquert''' ([[Düsseldorf]], 21 November 1962),  is a Spanish [[physicist]] recognized for his research in [[solar energy conversion]] and functional electronic devices. His work has significantly contributed to the development of [[perovskite solar cells]] and [[neuromorphic engineering|neuromorphic devices]] based on materials with memory properties, with applications in [[bioinspired computing]]. He was the founder and director (2015–2020) of the [[Institute of Advanced Materials (INAM)]] at the [[Universitat Jaume I]], and since 2017 he has presided over the [[Fundació Scito]] (Valencia). He is currently Distinguished Researcher at the [https://itq.upv-csic.es Instituto de Tecnología Química] (ITQ)<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Instituto de Tecnología Química (ITQ) |url=https://itq.upv-csic.es}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> a joint center of the [[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]] and the [[Universitat Politècnica de València|UPV]]

== Biography ==

Juan Bisquert was born in [[Düsseldorf]] ([[Germany]]) and grew up in [[Dénia]], in the [[Valencian Community]]. He earned a degree in [[physics]] from the [[University of Valencia|Universitat de València]], where he obtained his PhD in 1991 with a dissertation on donor–acceptor type semiconducting polymers.

He began his academic career at the [[University of Castilla-La Mancha]], on the [[Albacete]] campus, where he taught from 1987 to 1991. That same year, he joined the [[Universitat Jaume I]] in [[Castelló de la Plana]], where he developed a long-standing teaching and research trajectory, first as associate professor and later as full professor of [[applied physics]]. At this university, he founded and directed the Institute of Advanced Materials (INAM) between 2015 and 2020.<ref name="INAM">{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=INAM – Institut de Materials Avançats |url=https://www.inam.uji.es}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In 2024, he was appointed Distinguished Researcher at the [[Instituto de Tecnología Química]] (ITQ), a joint center of the [[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]] and the [[Universitat Politècnica de València|UPV]], where he currently leads the research group PROFUND (Processing Functional Ionic-Electronic Devices), focused on the development of functional materials for [[renewable energy]] and [[artificial intelligence]], with an emphasis on photoactive and memristive devices with ionic–electronic coupling.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=PROFUND – Processing Functional Ionic-Electronic Devices |url=https://profund.itq.webs.upv.es}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

Since 2017, he has chaired the [[Fundació Scito]], an entity dedicated to the promotion of scientific and technological knowledge, through which he leads the international scientific conference platform [[nanoGe]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Fundació Scito |url=https://www.scito.org}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=nanoGe – Scientific Conferences |url=https://www.nanoge.org}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

== Research activity ==

Juan Bisquert has conducted extensive research in the field of [[solar energy conversion]], [[functional materials]], and electronic devices with dynamic response. At the [[Universitat Jaume I]], he served as director of the [[Institute of Advanced Materials (INAM)]], where he led studies on materials, [[nanostructures]], and devices for the production of [[clean energy]], with a particular focus on technologies such as [[perovskite solar cells]].<ref name="INAM" />

Among his most notable contributions is the application of the concept of [[quantum capacitance]] (also referred to as chemical capacitance) in nanostructured conductive devices, as well as the analysis of inductive and capacitive hysteresis phenomena in photoactive systems. These approaches have been essential to understanding the electrical dynamics and memory effects in solar cells and [[memristors]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |publisher=CRC Press |title=Nanostructured Energy Devices: Equilibrium Concepts and Kinetics |url=https://www.crcpress.com/Nanostructured-Energy-Devices-Equilibrium-Concepts-and-Kinetics/Bisquert/p/book/9781439836026}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

Bisquert has published more than 400 scientific articles in indexed international journals<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Juan Bisquert – Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=-TTRG2kAAAAJ}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and has been cited over 40,000 times. Since 2014, he has been continuously included in the list of Highly Cited Researchers by [[Clarivate Analytics]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Highly Cited Researchers |url=https://clarivate.com/highly-cited-researchers/}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

He is the European editor of the journal ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters]]'', published by the [[American Chemical Society]],<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters – ACS Publications |url=https://pubs.acs.org/journal/jpclcd}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref> and has served on the editorial boards of journals such as ''ChemElectroChem'' and ''Journal of Environmental Science and Sustainable Energy''.

He is the author of the book ''The Physics of Solar Energy Conversion'', which integrates his research on the physico-chemical principles of energy conversion technologies, with particular attention to solar cells and functional materials.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |publisher=Routledge |title=The Physics of Solar Energy Conversion |url=https://www.routledge.com/The-Physics-of-Solar-Energy-Conversion/Bisquert/p/book/9780367496029}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

In recent years, his research has focused on the development of [[memristor|memristive]] and [[neuromorphic engineering|neuromorphic]] devices for [[bioinspired computing]], integrating memory, learning, and signal processing functionalities. This line of work is part of the European project ''PeroSpiker'', funded by the [[European Research Council|ERC]], in which he serves as principal investigator. The project explores [[spiking neural network|spiking network]] architectures using devices based on [[perovskites]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=PeroSpiker – ERC Advanced Grant |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101097688}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=PeroSpiker Community – Zenodo |url=https://zenodo.org/communities/perospiker/records}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

His group investigates devices that combine ionic and electronic conduction, such as memristors and hybrid transistors, with complex dynamic responses—including hysteresis, bifurcations, and adaptive behavior—that enable the emulation of artificial neuron functions in bioinspired circuits. One of the models developed, CALM (Conductance-Activated Quasi-Linear Memristor), describes the gradual activation of conductance through coupled electronic and ionic transitions.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Kinetics of Volatile and Nonvolatile Halide Perovskite Devices – The CALM Model |url=https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03132}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>

This approach has been presented in scientific publications and international conferences such as ''Neuronics25'', featuring research on the dynamic properties of neuromorphic memristors and oscillators, [[impedance spectroscopy]], and [[Hopf bifurcation|Hopf-type bifurcations]] applied to the modeling of artificial neurons.<ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Neuronics 2025 – Conference on Bioinspired Technologies |url=https://www.nanoge.org/Neuronics25/home}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref><ref>{{cite web|access-date=29 July 2025 |title=Dynamical Properties of Neuromorphic Memristors and Oscillators – Neuronics25 |url=https://doi.org/10.29363/nanoge.neuronics.2025.010}}<!-- auto-translated from Spanish by Module:CS1 translator --></ref>
